capabilities: Open JSON, CSV, Python, YAML and other text files in normal Obsidian tabs
Edit files with syntax highlighting, find and replace, undo/redo and multiple selections
Preview CSV files as read-only Markdown-styled tables and edit the source on demand
Auto-save after typing pauses and reload external changes with conflict banners
Register file extensions and open extensionless or dot files via command
disambiguation: Despite the name, it edits files, not just views them: it supports source editing, find and replace, and auto-save.
extras: Requires Obsidian 1.13.0 or later. Refuses non-UTF-8 encodings and binary formats; files over 20 MiB cannot be opened and syntax highlighting is dropped above 1,048,576 characters; CSV preview caps at 500 rows and 100 columns.
motivation: The author wanted a deliberately minimal alternative to existing plugins that open many file kinds with extensive editing features.
problem: Obsidian cannot open many text file types natively, and existing multi-format plugins are heavyweight; this plugin offers a small, focused way to read and edit plain text files.
summary: Minimal text file viewer and editor that opens JSON, CSV, Python and other text files in Obsidian tabs with syntax highlighting and auto-save.
